body.x: HMB Co., Ltd. (CEO Jeong Jeongil) announced its participation in CES 2025, scheduled from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas, to exhibit at the K-Startup Pavilion.

Founded to combine healthcare and renewable energy, HMB secured a patent for a "Smart Natural Lighting System for Healthcare and Renewable Energy." Since then, the company has aimed to provide renewable energy systems across various industries, promoting environmental sustainability.

At CES 2025, HMB will unveil its innovative AI-driven self-diagnostic home healthcare system. The system comprises a device capable of capturing ear, nose, oral cavity, teeth, and skin images, along with a mobile application for hardware control and data monitoring.

The system leverages an AI server to analyze user-uploaded images by comparing them against a database of over 50,000 pre-learned images. The results are presented alongside three comparable images, offering actionable insights for users to manage their health proactively. This includes recommendations for treatment methods, suitable medications, and accessible healthcare facilities, ultimately enhancing personal access to medical services.

The device features advanced sensors that measure indoor temperature and humidity, surface and core object temperatures, and other environmental data. This capability enables users to monitor factors such as children’s fever and indoor air quality, optimizing health management and maintaining overall household wellness.

HMB's system also stands out with its user-friendly interface and mobile app accessibility. It allows users of all ages to utilize its features without difficulty, regardless of location or time constraints.

An HMB representative stated, "Our AI self-diagnostic home healthcare system will be a pivotal platform within the industry. By providing personalized health management insights through advanced AI analysis, we anticipate significant interest from the global healthcare market."

The representative added, "At CES, we aim to demonstrate the system's capabilities to key players across healthcare, technology, and lifestyle industries. We also plan to explore partnerships and investment opportunities while showcasing the system's global potential. Our long-term vision includes empowering individual health management and contributing to sustainable global healthcare systems."

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
